access_notes.value: You must register as an SP-API developer (developer profile with roles). Public developers need a publicly accessible website, must list in the Selling Partner Appstore, and are reviewed by Amazon; requesting restricted (PII) roles triggers a further architecture review with the SP-API Solutions Architecture team. Private applications for your own organization can be self-authorized against your own selling partner account, but a selling partner (Seller/Vendor Central) account is still required.

verdict_reason: SP-API is a broad, publicly documented REST API with OAuth 2.0 (LWA), SDKs, sandbox variants, and notifications. However, credentials are gated: developers must register an SP-API developer profile, public apps need a website and Appstore listing and are reviewed by Amazon, and restricted/PII roles require an additional architecture review. That review/role-approval gate makes it moderate rather than easy.
main_blocker: Amazon developer-profile/app review and role approval (architecture review for PII roles)
outreach_reason: Public developer registration is subject to Amazon's review, and restricted-role access requires an architecture review with the SP-API Solutions Architecture team, so a human-facing application/review step is required for broader access.
open_questions: Whether a Professional (paid) selling account is required before registering as a developer is not stated in the captured sources; Seller Central forum snippets hint at plan implications but were not fetched.

Official_mcp_server value comes from Anthropic's Claude connector listing (third-party) reporting the amazon.com-hosted endpoint https://sellingpartner-ai.amazon.com/mcp; Amazon's own docs in the bundle only describe the Selling Partner plugin (beta) without publishing the MCP endpoint.
Numeric per-operation rate limits exist in per-API references but were not captured; only token-bucket throttling is confirmed by the evidence.
SDK list may be incomplete: a Python SDK tutorial URL surfaced in the search index but its page text was not fetched; the bundle only confirms Java and C# tutorials.
A github.com/amzn/selling-partner-agentic-toolkit repo surfaced in search results but was not fetched, so it is not listed as a community MCP server.
SP-API 'scopes' are implemented as roles; whether Amazon publishes OAuth scope strings per se (versus role-based permissions) is not explicitly evidenced.
The Amazon Ads MCP Server is a separate advertising product and was not treated as the SP-API MCP server.
